cwe_name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code sends a client-controlled 'substitute' parameter (400px) to server-side image processing, but CWE-770 requires demonstration of unbounded resource allocation, not just parameter passing

connection.evidence: Client-controlled substituteImg boolean and fixed value 400 are sent via fm.request() to server-side 'dim' command handler for image processing

diff_causality.evidence: The added line introduces the substitute parameter transmission, but the resource allocation mechanism exists server-side; this change enables/disables the parameter flow

security_control.required_control: Resource allocation limits and throttling for image processing operations
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-770 requires controls to prevent unbounded resource consumption during image processing operations
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No evidence of server-side bounds checking on the substitute parameter value; client sends fixed 400px but server processing limits are unknown

concrete_impact.evidence: No demonstrated resource exhaustion; substitute parameter is fixed at 400px when enabled, which is a moderate value unlikely to cause significant resource allocation

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the substitute parameter would not be sent to the server, preventing any server-side processing based on this client-controlled value.
supporting_evidence: Client constructs server request with 'substitute' parameter controlling server-side image processing
substituteImg boolean derived from configuration and file size thresholds enables parameter transmission
contradicting_evidence: Substitute parameter value is fixed at 400px when enabled, not client-controlled arbitrary values
Multiple client-side thresholds (file.size > options.dimSubImgSize, file.size > options.getDimThreshold) limit when this parameter is sent
unresolved_facts: Server-side validation and bounds checking on substitute parameter
Actual resource allocation behavior of server-side image processing
Whether substitute parameter value can be manipulated to cause resource exhaustion
